item.title: [LU-18857] tunable parameter to allow/deny new MDT/OST registration with MGS
item.description:
It would be useful to have tunable parameters on the MGS to enable/disable new filesystem registrations, as well as new MDT and OST registrations to an existing filesystem, so that it isn't possible to accidentally add new targets into an existing filesystem.

There should be a top-level parameter, like mgs.allow_register, that controls whether a new filesystem can be registered. There should be a per-filesystem parameter, maybe mgs.FSNAME.allow_register (or part of mgs.MGS.live.FSNAME?) that controls whether a new MDT or OST target can register with the filesystem.

The allow_register parameters should have a few different states:

  • disable all new registrations, which is the most secure, but may be inconvenient for some sites/users if they are not aware of this
  • configurable time-limited window for registrations (e.g. 1h) sufficient for configuring a new filesystem, but then reverting automatically to the "disable all new registrations" mode.
  • allow all new registrations, which would be equivalent to the current behavior. This may just be a long window (e.g. 2^30s) to simplify the state management.

This would be similar to the WiFi Protected Setup (WPS) button on a WiFi router, to allow new connections for a short window, while keeping the system in a "default secure" mode most of the time.

It seems reasonable to have the top-level default for be "1h since MGS was formatted/writeconf", and the filesystem default be something like "1h since the filesystem configuration was added on the MGS". This should be enough time to add all of the new MDTs/OSTs to a filesystem, to avoid causing issues for admins that are not aware of this parameter.

If the registration window has expired and a new target attempts to join a configuration, then the MGS should print a very clear message on the console for what parameter needs to be set in order to register a new filesystem or target.

For Lustre configuration tools, they could set allow_register with a short window for the occasions a new OSTs/MDTs is added, and then (optionally) manually disable it again after the configuration change was completed if the window had not expired. This would be more robust than enabling allow_register permanently and then disabling it afterward, in case the tool itself had a failure in the middle and was unable to disable it.

status.description: This issue was once resolved, but the resolution was deemed incorrect. From here issues are either marked assigned or resolved.

comments.comment: For new MDT/OST registrations, one addition to a time-based window setting, which acts as a "timeout", could be that an enabled allow_register is automatically disabled as soon as a client mounts the file system. This could allow a longer time-limited window since it guarantees that the setting is not accidentally left enabled.

IIUC the use case is for multiple filesystems, where this control would prevent accidentally adding a new storage target to the wrong filesystem ?

The use case is to prevent any kind of accidental (or potentially malicious) addition of new targets to the filesystem after the filesystem is initially set up.  A tool like EMF would easily be able to set allow_register=1 before adding targets, and set it to 0 immediately after they have successfully registered.

This has been an ongoing (though intermittent) issue in our test environment, where filesystems are all named "lustre", and some old VM that was not rebooted tries to add itself to the new filesystem running on peer nodes, though there is separate work underway to test with random filesystem names to mitigate this.

In production environments, it is occasionally the case that a second filesystem is added with the same fsname when it is intended to be a new filesystem, or a fat-finger "fs01" instead of "fs02" might happen and immediately add new targets to the old filesystem (which would be much more laborious to undo).

There have been several cases I saw recently where a test cluster failed because some random IP address added itself to the filesystem.

It would be useful (as a follow-on patch) to set allow_register with some short timeout (e.g. 5m or whatever the minimum reasonable time is to allow all MDTs and OSTs to mount after the MGS is first mounted) in test-framework.sh::start("mgs") for most of the test scripts. This will allow the MGS to block external hosts from adding themselves to the filesystem.

There would definitely be some subtest cases in conf-sanity.sh where allow_register=N might need to be set again for some short interval (=60s?) to expand the filesystem (e.g. add OSTs) if it wasn't just reformatted, but that would be the exception rather than the rule, and could be found by trial and error.

It would make sense to enable this on a script-by-script basis so that they can be tested separately (especially conf-sanity.sh that has a lot of reformatting) and then landed incremnetally when ready. That will "protect" an increasing fraction of the testing as the patches land, and will also provide good test coverage for this feature.

Hi adilger,

How are we planning to implement this?

One approach I can think of is to extend start_mgs to accept a timeout value, for example:

start_mgs <TIMEOUT>

Alternatively, we could set an environment variable before starting the MGS and add a check in start() or similar to see if the variable is present. If it is, the specified timeout could be enforced during startup.

What do you think about this approach?

I don't have a specific plan, but some ideas that come to mind:

  • set a timeout for connections at first MGS startup, which is long enough to mount the MDTs and OSTs (based on $MDSCOUNT and $OSTCOUNT)
  • allow MGS connections when new targets are formatted, and disable them after all MDTs and OSTs have been mounted, and fix the test cases that have issues.

Pushed the improved version check patches to b_es6_0 and b_es7_0 branch.  Although the final version checks will be updated after https://review.whamcloud.com/c/fs/lustre-release/+/63425 lands, that change is still under review and may take some time to merge.
